message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Masterful atmosphere, iconic performances, psychological terror. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | Suspenseful paranoia, practical effects that still look terrifying. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez | Found‑footage innovation, immersive dread. |
| 2001 | **28 Days Later…** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑moving zombie outbreak, gritty realism. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Dark, twisted moral dilemmas, cult‑classic status. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found footage that made a huge impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Strong storytelling, effective scares, and a solid franchise foundation. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | Meta‑take on horror tropes, clever twists. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | Original premise, creepy soundtrack, unsettling vibe. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | Period authenticity, slow‑burn dread, atmospheric tension. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | Social commentary meets horror, sharp satire. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | Silence as a weapon, emotional stakes. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | Daylight horror, unsettling folk rituals. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Modern retelling, psychological thriller elements. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** | Nia DaCosta | Reimagined myth, strong social themes. |
| 2022 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | New setting, visceral gore, fun for gore‑hungry fans. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | Gerard Johnstone | AI horror with a twist, commentary on tech addiction. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or sci‑fi horror. Enjoy the chills!
